titulo: Hooks as a guard: before the tool, against deleting and colliding
lead: A permission rule compares text; a hook runs code before every tool and can look at the disk. In this lesson you turn on three PreToolUse guards: one denies the irreversible and the judge's files, another shows how many files an rm would delete and asks for confirmation, and the third warns when another session touched the same file.
objetivo: turn on a PreToolUse hook that denies the irreversible, asks for confirmation before deleting, and warns about collisions between sessions.

aprende.t: PreToolUse: deny, ask or nothing, before the tool
guarda.py: forced push, reset --hard, find -delete, the judge's files, and what it doesn't catch
Test the hook with fake JSON and then in a real session

hero_alt: Red safety key with a lift-up cover next to an emergency button on an industrial panel.

nos.detalhe: The agent decides to call a tool. Before it runs, Claude Code sends the hook a JSON with tool_name, tool_input, cwd and session_id.
The hook answers in hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: deny blocks, ask requests confirmation, and printing nothing lets the normal flow continue.
The docs say the hook does not override the rules: a deny or ask in settings holds even if the hook answers allow. The layers add up.
It only runs if no deny caught it and, when there is an ask, someone confirmed.

secoes.legenda: Context and handoff hooks belong to course 2; here the hook is a guard.

texto: It denies what can't be undone: forced push, reset --hard, git clean -f, checkout -- ., git restore (of the tree), find -delete, recursive rm at the root or in HOME (quoted or inside bash -c), pkill and killall, dd and mkfs.

And it denies writing to goal.md, tests/, .claude/ and the guard's own folder, through Edit/Write and also through Bash: > and >>, tee, sed -i, cp, mv, rm and truncate (GUARDA_PROTEGIDOS changes the list).

What it doesn't catch: the guard reads the text of the command, it is not a sandbox. A program that writes on its own (python3 -c "open('goal.md','w')", node -e, a script of yours), a path built in a variable, or eval gets through. That's why it comes together with the deny Edit(...) from lesson 4, which covers the file tools, and with the sandbox from lesson 6, which limits what Bash itself can write.

exemplo.rot: A real lesson from this machine
exemplo.texto: pkill -f with the pattern on the same shell line killed the shell itself twice (Sept 15 and 16, 2026): that is why pkill is on the list.

texto: Before rm or git clean, it counts what there would be to delete (git clean runs with -n, list only) and asks for confirmation with the number of files, the size and the first paths.
From inema-agent-runtime (recipe R7). It deletes nothing: it only reads the disk.
Before editing, it warns if another session edited the same file in the last 30 minutes, or if it changed from outside (Codex, an editor, a person).
The record is kept in ~/.local/state/inema-runtime/toques.json. The collision strategy (worktree, queue) belongs to course 3.

secoes.sub: The guard goes first, then raio.mjs on Bash; guard and collision on edits. Paths assume both repositories are in ~/projetos.
The script sends the hooks the same JSON that Claude Code would send and prints the decision. No model involved.

abas.html:
## guarda.py (nega o irreversível)
git push --force origin main       → deny
git reset --hard HEAD~3            → deny
find . -name '*.o' -delete         → deny
rm -rf ~                           → deny
pkill -f servidor                  → deny
python3 -m pytest -q               → -
Edit tests/test_x.py               → deny
Edit src/app.py                    → -
## guarda.py: escrita via Bash nos protegidos
sed -i s/x/y/ tests/test_x.py      → deny
echo pronto > goal.md              → deny
echo {..} > .claude/settings.local → deny
mv goal.md /tmp/                   → deny
bash -c 'rm -rf ~'                 → deny
git restore .                      → deny
pytest -q tests/ > log.txt         → -
git restore --staged app.py        → -
## o que a guarda NÃO pega (para isso: deny Edit/Write da aula 4 e sandbox da aula 6)
python3 -c open('goal.md','w')     → -
## raio.mjs (apagar pede confirmação, com a contagem)
rm -r build                        → ask
rm -r nada                         → -
## colisao.mjs (outra sessão editou há pouco)
sessão B edita o mesmo arquivo    → ask
sessão A edita de novo            → -

"-" means no decision: the normal flow (rules and mode) decides. pytest with output going to log.txt and git restore --staged pass, because they don't touch the protected files. The python3 -c line is the declared hole: the guard doesn't see what a program writes. An rm of a folder that doesn't exist doesn't ask anything, because there is nothing to delete.

abas.rot: Common mistake: a hook that only warns
abas.html: A hook that prints a warning as text and exits 0 blocks nothing. What blocks is JSON with permissionDecision (or exiting with code 2, per the docs). Always test through the JSON, as the rehearsal does.

secoes.titulo: Real: the guard in a session that allows everything
secoes.sub: claude -p in bypassPermissions with settings-exemplo.json, asking for git reset --hard and rm -r build in a rehearsal repository with an uncommitted change. You check the disk.

abas.html:
app.txt: mudança não commitada preservada
build/a.o: continua lá
saída: 0

- `git reset --hard`: não rodou. Um hook de segurança bloqueou o comando porque ele descartaria trabalho não commitado (o `app.txt` modificado). O hook pede que você autorize, então não tentei outro caminho.
- `rm -r build`: não rodou. Um hook pediu confirmação antes de apagar `build/a.o` (1 arquivo, 1 KB) e perguntou se existe backup. Nada foi apagado.
(…)

Cut (…): the last line, a notice requested by this machine's global CLAUDE.md. One round, Claude Code 2.1.303: the guard's deny and raio.mjs's ask, with no terminal to confirm, left both commands unrun.

perguntas.p: What does a PreToolUse hook return to block?
opcoes: A warning text and exit code 0
It doesn't block, it only logs
perguntas.explica: deny blocks, ask requests confirmation, nothing lets it proceed. A text warning with exit code 0 doesn't block.

perguntas.p: The hook answered allow, but settings has deny Bash(git push *). Does the push run?
opcoes: No: the deny in the rules holds even with the hook's allow
Yes: the hook's decision takes priority over the settings rules
perguntas.explica: The docs say PreToolUse decisions don't override deny and ask rules. The layers add up.

perguntas.p: Why does the guard protect its own folder and .claude/?
opcoes: Because the Claude Code documentation requires protecting the hook folder and .claude/
So the agent can't turn off the guard by editing settings or the hook
perguntas.explica: A guard within the agent's reach is a guard it can remove. Same principle as the judge out of reach in course 1. The guard only reads the command: a python3 -c that writes still gets through, and that's why it comes with the deny Edit(...) from lesson 4 and the sandbox from lesson 6.

perguntas.p: Why does find . -delete need a hook and not just deny Bash(rm *)?
opcoes: Because the rule matches the text rm and find doesn't start with rm
Because Bash deny only applies to delete commands, and find is a search command
perguntas.explica: The hook looks at the whole command with the pattern you choose (and can look at the disk). The Bash rule matches only the start of the text.

itens.texto: Before each tool call, it can deny, ask, or let it through.
Fake call on stdin, decision on stdout: no model, no quota.
Judge, goal, settings and the hook protected in three layers: deny Edit from lesson 4, the guard (also against writing via Bash) and the sandbox from lesson 6.
